source.title: Differential fear conditioning generates prefrontal neural ensembles of safety signals

confidence_rationale: Activity-dependent ensemble mapping shows the prelimbic mPFC codes context-danger associations while differential conditioning recruits additional PL+IL ensembles tied to inhibition of generalized fear -- i.e. learned context-safety is an active prefrontal representation, not mere absence of threat. Directly supports MECH-303's prefrontal substrate for a contextual passive safety store (IL expression gating; cortical contextual representation). Source quality good (ensemble-level mapping, behavioural discrimination). Mapping fidelity moderate-high: Corches evidences the prefrontal/contextual safety substrate but does not isolate the slow diffuse contextual-exposure update rule MECH-303 specifies, nor the vHipp-PL store. Transfer risk moderate (rodent differential fear conditioning to REE context-safety representation).
failure_signatures: PL codes context-DANGER and IL/PL code inhibition of GENERALIZED fear -- if REE collapsed safety into a single 'low-harm' scalar, it would miss that danger-monitoring and safety-discrimination are separable prefrontal ensembles.

Safety here is built by differential conditioning (discriminating a safe-but-similar cue from a dangerous one), not by passive non-occurrence alone -- a pure passive-exposure update rule (MECH-303 as written) may under-specify the discrimination demand this paper documents.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Prefrontal neuronal ensembles code functional context-danger and context-safety relationships: the prelimbic mPFC monitors context-danger associations to conditioned fear, while differential conditioning sparks additional PL and IL ensembles associated with the inhibition of generalized fear; safety learning is active prefrontal representation that is gradually updated and rebalanced.
mapping.ree_translation: MECH-303: a context-bound passive safety representation ('this environment predicts absence of suffering') with a prefrontal substrate (IL for expression gating). Corches grounds the prefrontal/contextual locus and confirms safety is an active learned representation distinct from the threat representation -- precisely the relief-vs-safety dissociation: safety is a prospective inhibitory predictor, not the offset reinforcement event of MECH-302.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Corches studies discriminative fear conditioning (distinguishing a safe similar cue from a dangerous one), which is closer to cue/context conditioned inhibition than to MECH-303's pure passive-exposure-without-harm update rule; it also does not test the vHipp-PL contextual store MECH-303 names. It supports the prefrontal safety substrate and the safety-as-active-representation premise, not MECH-303's specific diffuse update dynamics.
mapping.source_context: Mouse, activity-dependent neuronal ensemble tagging (Mayford TetTag-style), differential auditory/contextual fear conditioning, PL/IL subdivisions of mPFC.

confidence_components.notes: Strong on the prefrontal safety locus and the danger/safety ensemble separation; the gap is between discriminative-conditioning safety (tested) and passive-contextual safety (MECH-303 as written). Weighted toward mapping_fidelity for this architectural claim.
